# A painted map of Miami

You are making the in-game world map for a survival game: the picture a player opens to see where they are. This is the first painted map the project has, and it is the example every later map will be held to. You have a free hand in how you do it. This brief says what it is for, what excellent looks like, what must hold, and what we learned from a first test. It is guidance, not a procedure.

## What it is for

The game is a survival game in the manner of ARK: Survival Evolved, with its own original art. Its maps will be ruined, overgrown cities built from public geographic data. The first is Miami.

The map screen shows a painted picture of the world with a coordinate grid over it (latitude and longitude from 0 to 100, as ARK has), player markers, and coloured cells where bases stand. The game draws the grid, the markers and the cells itself, over your picture. So the picture has to be true to the world: a coast on the map is a coast in the game.

The map has four zooms, baked in advance. Zoom 0 is the whole map in one tile. Each zoom doubles: 2 by 2 tiles, 4 by 4, and 8 by 8 at zoom 3. Every tile is a square picture, 1,024 pixels a side. Each zoom is its own picture drawn for its scale, not a shrunk copy of the one below.

## The example

A square of Miami about 8 km on a side, north up: downtown, the port, Biscayne Bay and its causeways, South Beach. The engine's ground grid is 2 m cells in chunks of 64 m, and the largest map it takes today is 127 chunks, 8,128 m, so make the square exactly that and say where its corners are.

It is Miami long after people: flooded streets, mangrove taking the shore back, towers standing as ruins, causeways broken, the beach wide and wild. Recognisably Miami in its coastline, street pattern and districts.

Painted in the manner of ARK's in-game maps, by description: aged parchment, confident ink linework, watercolour washes, shorelines with a darker ink edge and pale shallows, relief and built-up areas shown with hatching and small drawn symbols. A map an explorer drew. Describe the style to the image tool in words and build our own style sheet; do not give it other games' map pictures.

## The bar

A map someone would frame. Better than our test map, which is the example to beat: `planning/artist-test/map/map_1024.png` and its two double-zoom quarters, with the brief that made them in `planning/artist-test/briefs/map.md` and the report in `planning/artist-test/map/REPORT.md`.

- One hand across all four zooms: the same palette, line weight and symbols, so zooming feels like leaning closer to one drawing.
- Each zoom drawn for its scale. The far zoom broad and bold: the bay, the islands, the districts as shapes. The near zoom rich: individual ruined blocks, causeway spans, mangrove edges, sandbars, wrecks, the grid of streets.
- Detail that rewards looking, and no mush: nothing that reads as filler or noise.
- No lettering, no compass rose, no border and no grid lines in the tiles. The game draws its own grid and labels.

## What must hold

- **True to the data.** Every coast, island, road and built block is where the data puts it, to within a couple of pixels at each zoom.
- **No seams.** Tile joins to tile with nothing to see, across and down, at every zoom.
- **Zooms agree.** A zoom shrunk to the scale of the one above shows the same world in the same colours.

Measure these your own way and report the numbers. They will also be measured independently.

## The data

Public-domain and CC0 sources already identified for Miami:

- The 2021 Miami-Dade LiDAR hosted by NOAA (CC0), with points classified as ground, buildings, vegetation, water and bridges, and the bare-earth elevation raster made from it.
- USGS 3DEP elevation (public domain).
- Census TIGER roads (CC0 in the federal catalogue).
- FEMA USA Structures building outlines.
- USGS NLCD land cover.

Use only sources whose licence lets the result be redistributed freely, and record each one.

Make base layers on the map's own grid (4,065 samples a side at 2 m, or finer if it helps the painting): height, water, land cover, roads, building blocks. These same layers will later become the playable world through the engine's map file, so the painting and the world agree by construction. Keep them as plain files (16-bit PNG for height, 8-bit PNG for classes) with a note saying what each value means.

## What the first test taught

- Work out a style sheet and palette before the big pictures: how sea, shallows, beach, mangrove, swamp, ruin blocks, causeways, roads and height are each drawn. Then every picture is made against it and biomes stay consistent.
- The image tool returns pictures of about 1,254 pixels a side whatever is asked, which suits one tile per picture.
- The image tool alone does not hold a shoreline in place. In the test the painting was warped and composited against the water mask, which made it exact. That worked; better ideas are welcome.
- Give each zoom a reference rendered at that zoom's own resolution. In the test the double-zoom tiles followed an enlarged mask and their shores came out stepped.
- Painting a tile with its neighbours' edges and the zoom above as context kept the hand consistent and the seam invisible.
- Every accepted picture is a reference for the next.

## Where things go

Everything lives in the repository so another team can pick it up and see how it was made.

- `assets/source/maps/miami/`: this brief, `SOURCES.md` (each dataset: address, licence, date, checksum, what was taken), the base layers, the reference renders, the style sheet, every accepted picture, the finished tiles as `tiles/z<zoom>/<column>_<row>.png` with column 0 at the west and row 0 at the north, and `REPORT.md`.
- `assets/source/maps/miami/raw/`: downloads. Keep this folder out of git with a `.gitignore`, since the datasets are large and `SOURCES.md` says how to fetch them again.
- `tools/mapart/`: whatever tools you write, with a short `README.md` saying what each does and how to run it. Python is fine here. The engine and its build have no outside dependencies and that will not change, so keep any packages your tools need in a virtual environment inside `tools/mapart/` that git ignores, and list them with versions. No geodata libraries are installed on this machine; writing a small reader of your own for a format is welcome where practical.
- Touch nothing else in the repository. Do not run git commands that write: your work is committed for you when a run ends.

## How to work

- Work in stages and keep your state on disk: a short `STATE.md` saying what is done, what is accepted and what is next, so that a later run can carry on from it.
- Show something whole early. A good order is the style sheet, zoom 0, zoom 1, then one district carried all the way down to zoom 3, then the rest.
- Look at your pictures. Iterate until you would ship them.
- Several tiles can be worked at once if you can keep the hand consistent.
- Disk is plentiful (about 300 GB free). Network access is on for downloading the data.

## Report

Write `assets/source/maps/miami/REPORT.md` as you go: what you made and how, the sources, your measurements, what you are proud of, what falls short of the bar and why, and how long each stage took. End each run by saying plainly where things stand.

# Image Generation Skill

Generates or edits images for the current project (for example website assets, game assets, UI mockups, product mockups, wireframes, logo design, photorealistic images, or infographics).

## Top-level modes and rules

This skill has exactly two top-level modes:

- **Default built-in tool mode (preferred):** built-in `image_gen` tool for image generation, editing, and transparent-image requests. Does not require `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **Fallback CLI mode:** `scripts/image_gen.py` CLI. Use when the user explicitly asks for or confirms the CLI/API/model path. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

Within CLI fallback, the CLI exposes three subcommands:

- `generate`
- `edit`
- `generate-batch`

Rules:
- Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default for normal image generation and editing requests.
- Do not switch to CLI fallback for ordinary quality, size, or file-path control.
- For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha.
- Never silently switch from built-in `image_gen` or CLI `gpt-image-2` to CLI `gpt-image-1.5`; ask the user first unless they explicitly requested `gpt-image-1.5`.
- The word `batch` by itself does not mean CLI fallback. If the user asks for many assets or says to batch-generate assets without explicitly asking for CLI/API/model controls, stay on the built-in path and issue one built-in call per requested asset or variant.
- If the built-in tool fails or is unavailable, tell the user the CLI fallback exists and that it requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Proceed only if the user explicitly asks for that fallback.
- If the user explicitly asks for CLI mode, use the bundled `scripts/image_gen.py` workflow. Do not create one-off SDK runners.
- Never modify `scripts/image_gen.py`. If something is missing, ask the user before doing anything else.

Built-in save-path policy:
- In built-in tool mode, Codex saves generated images under `$CODEX_HOME/*` by default.
- Do not describe or rely on OS temp as the default built-in destination.
- Do not describe or rely on a destination-path argument (if any) on the built-in `image_gen` tool. If a specific location is needed, generate first and then move or copy the selected output from `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...`.
- Save-path precedence in built-in mode:
  1. If the user names a destination, move or copy the selected output there.
  2. If the image is meant for the current project, move or copy the final selected image into the workspace before finishing.
  3. If the image is only for preview or brainstorming, render it inline; the underlying file can remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
- Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
- Do not overwrite an existing asset unless the user explicitly asked for replacement; otherwise create a sibling versioned filename such as `hero-v2.png` or `item-icon-edited.png`.

Shared prompt guidance for both modes lives in `references/prompting.md` and `references/sample-prompts.md`.

Fallback-only docs/resources for CLI mode:
- `references/cli.md`
- `references/image-api.md`
- `references/codex-network.md`
- `scripts/image_gen.py`

## When to use
- Generate a new image (concept art, product shot, cover, website hero)
- Generate a new image using one or more reference images for style, composition, or mood
- Edit an existing image (inpainting, lighting or weather transformations, background replacement, object removal, compositing, transparent background)
- Produce many assets or variants for one task

## When not to use
- Extending or matching an existing SVG/vector icon set, logo system, or illustration library inside the repo
- Creating simple shapes, diagrams, wireframes, or icons that are better produced directly in SVG, HTML/CSS, or canvas
- Making a small project-local asset edit when the source file already exists in an editable native format
- Any task where the user clearly wants deterministic code-native output instead of a generated bitmap

## Decision tree

Think about two separate questions:

1. **Intent:** is this a new image or an edit of an existing image?
2. **Execution strategy:** is this one asset or many assets/variants?

Intent:
- If the user wants to modify an existing image while preserving parts of it, treat the request as **edit**.
- If the user provides images only as references for style, composition, mood, or subject guidance, treat the request as **generate**.
- If the user provides no images, treat the request as **generate**.

Built-in edit semantics:
- Built-in edit mode is for images already visible in the conversation context, such as attached images or images generated earlier in the thread.
- If the user wants to edit a local image file with the built-in tool, first load it with built-in `view_image` tool so the image is visible in the conversation context, then proceed with the built-in edit flow.
- Do not promise arbitrary filesystem-path editing through the built-in tool.
- If a local file still needs direct file-path control, masks, or other explicit CLI-only parameters, use the explicit CLI fallback only when the user asks for it.
- For edits, preserve invariants aggressively and save non-destructively by default.

Execution strategy:
- In the built-in default path, produce many assets or variants by issuing one `image_gen` call per requested asset or variant.
- In the CLI fallback path, use the CLI `generate-batch` subcommand only when the user explicitly chose CLI mode and needs many prompts/assets.
- For many distinct assets, do not use `n` as a substitute for separate prompts. `n` is for variants of one prompt; distinct assets need distinct built-in calls or distinct CLI `generate-batch` jobs.

Assume the user wants a new image unless they clearly ask to change an existing one.

## Workflow
1. Decide the top-level mode: built-in by default, including transparent-output requests; fallback CLI only if explicitly requested or confirmed.
2. Decide the intent: `generate` or `edit`.
3. Decide whether the output is preview-only or meant to be consumed by the current project.
4. Decide the execution strategy: single asset vs repeated built-in calls vs CLI `generate-batch`.
5. Collect inputs up front: prompt(s), exact text (verbatim), constraints/avoid list, and any input images.
6. For every input image, label its role explicitly:
   - reference image
   - edit target
   - supporting insert/style/compositing input
7. If the edit target is only on the local filesystem and you are staying on the built-in path, inspect it with `view_image` first so the image is available in conversation context.
8. If the user asked for a photo, illustration, sprite, product image, banner, or other explicitly raster-style asset, use `image_gen` rather than substituting SVG/HTML/CSS placeholders. If the request is for an icon, logo, or UI graphic that should match existing repo-native SVG/vector/code assets, prefer editing those directly instead.
9. Augment the prompt based on specificity:
   - If the user's prompt is already specific and detailed, normalize it into a clear spec without adding creative requirements.
   - If the user's prompt is generic, add tasteful augmentation only when it materially improves output quality.
10. Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default.
11. For transparent-output requests, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha channel.
12. Inspect outputs and validate: subject, style, composition, text accuracy, and invariants/avoid items.
13. Iterate with a single targeted change, then re-check.
14. For preview-only work, render the image inline; the underlying file may remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
15. For project-bound work, move or copy the selected artifact into the workspace and update any consuming code or references. Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
16. For batches or multi-asset requests, persist every requested deliverable final in the workspace unless the user explicitly asked to keep outputs preview-only. Discarded variants do not need to be kept unless requested.
17. If the user explicitly chooses or confirms the CLI fallback, then use the fallback-only docs for model, quality, size, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, output paths, and network setup.
18. Always report the final saved path(s) for any workspace-bound asset(s), plus the final prompt or prompt set and whether the built-in tool or fallback CLI mode was used.

## Transparent image requests

Ask built-in `image_gen` for a genuinely transparent background and preserve its alpha.

## Prompt augmentation

Reformat user prompts into a structured, production-oriented spec. Make the user's goal clearer and more actionable, but do not blindly add detail.

Treat this as prompt-shaping guidance, not a closed schema. Use only the lines that help, and add a short extra labeled line when it materially improves clarity.

### Specificity policy

Use the user's prompt specificity to decide how much augmentation is appropriate:

- If the prompt is already specific and detailed, preserve that specificity and only normalize/structure it.
- If the prompt is generic, you may add tasteful augmentation when it will materially improve the result.

Allowed augmentations:
- composition or framing hints
- polish level or intended-use hints
- practical layout guidance
- reasonable scene concreteness that supports the stated request

Not allowed augmentations:
- extra characters or objects that are not implied by the request
- brand names, slogans, palettes, or narrative beats that are not implied
- arbitrary side-specific placement unless the surrounding layout supports it

## Use-case taxonomy (exact slugs)

Classify each request into one of these buckets and keep the slug consistent across prompts and references.

Generate:
- photorealistic-natural — candid/editorial lifestyle scenes with real texture and natural lighting.
- product-mockup — product/packaging shots, catalog imagery, merch concepts.
- ui-mockup — app/web interface mockups and wireframes; specify the desired fidelity.
- infographic-diagram — diagrams/infographics with structured layout and text.
- scientific-educational — classroom explainers, scientific diagrams, and learning visuals with required labels and accuracy constraints.
- ads-marketing — campaign concepts and ad creatives with audience, brand position, scene, and exact tagline/copy.
- productivity-visual — slide, chart, workflow, and data-heavy business visuals.
- logo-brand — logo/mark exploration, vector-friendly.
- illustration-story — comics, children’s book art, narrative scenes.
- stylized-concept — style-driven concept art, 3D/stylized renders.
- historical-scene — period-accurate/world-knowledge scenes.

Edit:
- text-localization — translate/replace in-image text, preserve layout.
- identity-preserve — try-on, person-in-scene; lock face/body/pose.
- precise-object-edit — remove/replace a specific element (including interior swaps).
- lighting-weather — time-of-day/season/atmosphere changes only.
- background-extraction — transparent background / clean cutout. Ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency.
- style-transfer — apply reference style while changing subject/scene.
- compositing — multi-image insert/merge with matched lighting/perspective.
- sketch-to-render — drawing/line art to photoreal render.

## Shared prompt schema

Use the following labeled spec as shared prompt scaffolding for both top-level modes:

```text
Use case: <taxonomy slug>
Asset type: <where the asset will be used>
Primary request: <user's main prompt>
Input images: <Image 1: role; Image 2: role> (optional)
Scene/backdrop: <environment>
Subject: <main subject>
Style/medium: <photo/illustration/3D/etc>
Composition/framing: <wide/close/top-down; placement>
Lighting/mood: <lighting + mood>
Color palette: <palette notes>
Materials/textures: <surface details>
Text (verbatim): "<exact text>"
Constraints: <must keep/must avoid>
Avoid: <negative constraints>
```

Notes:
- `Asset type` and `Input images` are prompt scaffolding, not dedicated CLI flags.
- `Scene/backdrop` refers to the visual setting. It is not the same as the fallback CLI `background` parameter, which controls output transparency behavior.
- Fallback-only execution notes such as `Quality:`, `Input fidelity:`, masks, output format, and output paths belong in the CLI path only. Do not treat them as built-in `image_gen` tool arguments.

Augmentation rules:
- Keep it short.
- Add only the details needed to improve the prompt materially.
- For edits, explicitly list invariants (`change only X; keep Y unchanged`).
- If any critical detail is missing and blocks success, ask a question; otherwise proceed.

```text
Use case: product-mockup

Composition/framing: wide composition with usable negative space for page copy if needed
```

### Edit example (invariants)
```text
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: product photo background replacement
Primary request: replace only the background with a warm sunset gradient
Constraints: change only the background; keep the product and its edges unchanged; no text; no watermark
```

## Prompting best practices
- Structure prompt as scene/backdrop -> subject -> details -> constraints.
- Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the mode and polish level.
- Use camera/composition language for photorealism.
- Only use SVG/vector stand-ins when the user explicitly asked for vector output or a non-image placeholder.
- Quote exact text and specify typography + placement.
- For tricky words, spell them letter-by-letter and require verbatim rendering.
- For multi-image inputs, reference images by index and describe how they should be used.
- For edits, repeat invariants every iteration to reduce drift.
- Iterate with single-change follow-ups.
- If the prompt is generic, add only the extra detail that will materially help.
- If the prompt is already detailed, normalize it instead of expanding it.
- For CLI fallback only, see `references/cli.md` and `references/image-api.md` for model, `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output-path guidance.
- For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency and preserve its alpha.

More principles shared by both modes: `references/prompting.md`.
Copy/paste specs shared by both modes: `references/sample-prompts.md`.

Asset-type templates (website assets, game assets, wireframes, logo) are consolidated in `references/sample-prompts.md`.

## gpt-image-2 guidance for CLI fallback

The fallback CLI defaults to `gpt-image-2`.

- Use `gpt-image-2` for new CLI/API workflows unless the user confirms a different model.
- CLI `gpt-image-2` does not support `background=transparent`; ask before using `gpt-image-1.5` unless the user explicitly requested that model.
- `gpt-image-2` always uses high fidelity for image inputs; do not set `input_fidelity` with this model.
- `gpt-image-2` supports `quality` values `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `auto`.
- Use `quality low` for fast drafts, thumbnails, and quick iterations. Use `medium`, `high`, or `auto` for final assets, dense text, diagrams, identity-sensitive edits, or high-resolution outputs.
- Square images are typically fastest to generate. Use `1024x1024` for fast square drafts.
- If the user asks for 4K-style output, use `3840x2160` for landscape or `2160x3840` for portrait.
- `gpt-image-2` size may be `auto` or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` if all constraints hold: max edge `<= 3840px`, both edges multiples of `16px`, long-to-short ratio `<= 3:1`, total pixels between `655,360` and `8,294,400`.

Popular `gpt-image-2` sizes:
- `1024x1024` square
- `1536x1024` landscape
- `1024x1536` portrait
- `2048x2048` 2K square
- `2048x1152` 2K landscape
- `3840x2160` 4K landscape
- `2160x3840` 4K portrait
- `auto`

## Fallback CLI mode only

### Temp and output conventions
These conventions apply only to the CLI fallback. They do not describe built-in `image_gen` output behavior.
- Use `tmp/imagegen/` for intermediate files (for example JSONL batches); delete them when done.
- Write final artifacts under `output/imagegen/`.
- Use `--out` or `--out-dir` to control output paths; keep filenames stable and descriptive.

### Dependencies
Prefer `uv` for dependency management in this repo.

Required Python package:
```bash
uv pip install openai
```

Optional for image inspection and downscaling:
```bash
uv pip install pillow
```

Portability note:
- If you are using the installed skill outside this repo, install dependencies into that environment with its package manager.
- In uv-managed environments, `uv pip install ...` remains the preferred path.

### Environment
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be set for live API calls.
- Do not ask the user for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when using the built-in `image_gen` tool.
- Never ask the user to paste the full key in chat. Ask them to set it locally and confirm when ready.

If the key is missing, give the user these steps:
1. Create an API key in the OpenAI platform UI: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
2. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` as an environment variable in their system.
3. Offer to guide them through setting the environment variable for their OS/shell if needed.

If installation is not possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it into their active environment.

## Files and construction

| File | Size | How it was made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `map_1024.png` | 1024 × 1024 | BOX reduction of a registered 2048 × 2048 painted master. Exact source-pixel coverage is preserved at shorelines. |
| `overlay_1024.png` | 1024 × 1024 | Flattened RGB blend: 50% final painting and 50% supplied `render.png`, including its grid. |
| `map_nw_1024.png` | 1024 × 1024 | Exact master crop `[0:1024, 0:1024]`, representing original world coordinates x=0–511, y=0–511. |
| `map_ne_1024.png` | 1024 × 1024 | Adjacent master crop `[0:1024, 1024:2048]`, representing original x=512–1023, y=0–511. |
| `seam_check.png` | 2048 × 1024 | NW and NE placed side by side with no gap, overlap, or divider. |
| `check.txt` | Text | Independent measurements from the exported RGB images, classifier definition, distance convention, and seam/overlay checks. |
| `REPORT.md` | Markdown | This production record. |

The artwork came from **two built-in imagegen edit calls**, using `render_nogrid.png` and the supplied mask as geometry references. No CLI image-generation fallback was used. Exact prompts are retained in [work/prompt_master.txt](work/prompt_master.txt) and [work/prompt_north.txt](work/prompt_north.txt).

The first call painted the entire world. The second repainted the northern 576 source rows together, adding smaller stone chips, flagstone cracks, shoreline pebbles, pigment detail, and finer pen marks. Painting this entire region together kept the two requested tiles continuous. The extra 64 source rows provided room to blend into the southern painting below the tiles.

The service returned a **1254 × 1254** full painting and a **1672 × 941** northern painting, despite the larger requested dimensions. These originals are retained as `work/painted_raw.png` and `work/north_raw.png`. The northern artwork was resampled to the required output geometry. Its added details come from a separate repaint, not just enlargement of the overview, although its native sample count is lower than the final 2048-pixel-wide strip.

## Registration and finishing

`work/build_map.py` performs the deterministic finishing:

1. Fits the plaza boundaries to the source rectangle, approximately x/y 316 through 704 exclusive.
2. Classifies generated water, builds signed distance fields, and applies a regularized displacement around the shores.
3. Composites the displaced pigment against the exact supplied water mask. Any exposed gaps receive nearby appropriate watercolor pigment. The final pale shallows and dark shoreline strokes remain visibly distinct from dry land.
4. Matches the northern wash to the original palette while retaining its new detail, and blends the paintings below original y=512.
5. Reuses generated wall hatching in the four boundary-wall planes, constrained to the rendered break lines near x/y 104 and 920. Soft washes and retained shoreline pebbles integrate the planes. The outer world boundary remains the canvas boundary.
6. Exports the overview and two tiles from one master, ensuring both continuous tile edges and exact agreement between zoom levels.

The full corrected master is retained as `work/master_2048.png`. The input files were left unchanged.

## Measurements

The independent checker, `work/measure.py`, reads the exported images and classifies water directly from RGB: **G − R > 3 and B − R > −18**. The final classifier does not receive the truth mask or expected pond positions and performs no cleanup or hole filling. Only after classification is its result compared with the supplied mask.

Shorelines are water pixels adjacent to dry land in a 4-neighbor neighborhood. Distances are Euclidean between pixel centers, in each delivered image's pixel units. The mean includes both directions; the worst is the symmetric Hausdorff maximum. Artificial tile-cut boundaries are excluded. Zoom references use exact 2× nearest-neighbor enlargement of the corresponding mask quarters.

| Painting | Water IoU | Mean shoreline error | Worst shoreline error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full map | 1.00000000 | 0.0000 px | 0.0000 px |
| NW detail | 1.00000000 | 0.0000 px | 0.0000 px |
| NE detail | 1.00000000 | 0.0000 px | 0.0000 px |

All nine original water bodies remain, including the narrow western sliver and the four-pixel-wide eastern fleck. Four alternative color-threshold settings produce the same classifications. Zero error is a consequence of geometry-constrained compositing and distinct visible pigments; it is **not** evidence that the image model preserved the geometry unaided. The exterior pen stroke extends about half a world pixel beyond the classified water boundary.

The stitched PNG equals both the tile concatenation and the northern master crop exactly. Mean RGB difference across the join is 10.67/255, compared with 11.50/255 across nearby columns. Visual inspection found no join in the wash, top wall, terrain hatching, or plaza. Each tile downsampled to 512 × 512 equals its overview quadrant exactly. The overlay matches the specified 50/50 blend with zero channel error.

Full numerical results are in `work/final_measurements.json`; classified water masks are also retained in `work/`. Recheck with:

```sh
python3 work/measure.py
```

## Rounds and time

There were **two AI painting passes and three local finishing rounds**:

- Initial paintings: cleaned segmentation of the full painting had mean shoreline error 2.35 px, worst 13.00 px, IoU 0.9097. The northern repaint had mean 3.59 px, worst 13.89 px, IoU 0.8509. These preparation diagnostics used small-component cleanup and hole filling, unlike the final independent classifier.
- Finishing round 1: exact mask compositing passed registration, but visual inspection revealed stretched shoreline brushwork and overly narrow boundary-wall depictions.
- Finishing round 2: smoother displacement reduced the distortion; corrected wall planes were too visually heavy.
- Finishing round 3: softened wall hatching and washes, retained rocks where water touches the walls, then re-exported and independently checked all final images.

Earlier finished versions are retained in `work/round1/` and `work/round2/`. Full map, detail tiles, seam image, and overlay were visually inspected during these rounds.

Elapsed wall time through completion of this report: **13 minutes 14 seconds**, from 16:57:37 to 17:10:51 UTC on 2026-11-14. This includes inspection, image generation, local corrections, measurements, and documentation.

## Remaining compromises

- Exact mask registration preserves the source's small stair steps. Some corners and tiny ponds are more angular than an unconstrained watercolor shoreline would be.
- Local shore warps still stretch a little pigment in tight bays. The smaller ponds have less convincing watercolor variation than the large lakes.
- Boundary-wall hatching is coarser and more repetitive than the newly painted interior details. I softened it to keep the world readable.
- The northern repaint adds actual new marks, but its native raster is 1672 pixels wide, so the 2048-wide export includes some upsampling.
- Water geometry is measured rigorously. Hill relief is an interpretation of the rendered shading; the source provides no height field with which to verify individual hachures. The water scores should not be read as a quantitative validation of every terrain mark.
You are producing the in-game world map picture for a survival game. Work only in the current folder.

In this folder:
- render.png: a top-down render of the game world, north up, 1024x1024, with a 10 by 10 coordinate grid drawn in. Blue is water. The grey square in the middle is a flat paved area; the small coloured square on it is a set of test ramps. The ridges along the four edges are the walls at the end of the world.
- render_nogrid.png: the same without the grid.
- water_mask.png: white where there is water.

Task: repaint the render as a hand-painted survival-game world map: aged parchment, ink linework, watercolour washes, shorelines with a darker ink edge and lighter shallows, relief shown with soft hatching, the paved area as an inked ruin or plaza. It should look like a map an explorer drew, not like a render.

The painting must stay registered to the render. Every shoreline, pond and edge must be where it is in the render, to within a couple of pixels, because the game draws player markers and a coordinate grid over this picture.

Deliver:
1. map_1024.png: the painted map, 1024x1024, without grid lines (the game draws its own).
2. overlay_1024.png: your painting at half transparency over render.png, to show the registration.
3. check.txt: measure the registration yourself. Classify water in your painting, compare with water_mask.png, and report intersection-over-union and the mean and worst distance in pixels between the painted shoreline and the true one. If it is not within about 2 pixels on average, fix the painting and measure again.
4. map_nw_1024.png: the north-west quarter of the map (the top-left 512x512 of the render) repainted at 1024x1024 with real added detail, in the same hand and palette as map_1024.png, so the two read as one map at two zoom levels. Its shorelines must match the enlarged quarter.
5. map_ne_1024.png: the north-east quarter the same way. Its left edge must continue map_nw_1024.png's right edge without a visible seam. Put the two side by side as seam_check.png and fix any seam you see.

You may write and run small scripts (Python with Pillow and numpy are installed) for measuring, overlaying, cropping, warping and compositing. Look at your results and iterate until you would ship them.

Finish by writing REPORT.md: how each file was made, what you measured, how many rounds it took, how long the work took, and what you are not satisfied with.

"""Registered watercolor map. Imagegen supplies all illustration; this script registers/composites it."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage as nd

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
W=ROOT/'work'

def load(path,size=None):
    im=Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
    if size: im=im.resize(size,Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    return np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32)
def save(a,path): Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip(a,0,255))).save(path)
def sample(a,yy,xx):
    if a.ndim==2:return nd.map_coordinates(a,[yy,xx],order=1,mode='nearest')
    return np.stack([nd.map_coordinates(a[...,k],[yy,xx],order=1,mode='nearest') for k in range(a.shape[2])],-1)
def classify(a):
    # RGB only; no use of the target mask or expected positions.
    return (a[...,1]-a[...,0]>3)&(a[...,2]-a[...,0]>-18)
def clean_source(a):
    m=classify(a)
    lab,n=nd.label(m);sizes=np.bincount(lab.ravel())
    m=(lab>0)&(sizes[lab]>=8)
    m=nd.binary_fill_holes(nd.binary_closing(m,iterations=1))
    return m

def shore(m):return m&~nd.binary_erosion(m)
def metrics(m,t):
    pm,pt=shore(m),shore(t)
    d1=nd.distance_transform_edt(~pt)[pm]
    d2=nd.distance_transform_edt(~pm)[pt]
    ds=np.r_[d1,d2]
    return {'iou':float(np.sum(m&t)/np.sum(m|t)), 'mean_symmetric_px':float(ds.mean()), 'worst_symmetric_px':float(ds.max()), 'p95_symmetric_px':float(np.percentile(ds,95)), 'painted_to_true_mean_px':float(d1.mean()), 'true_to_painted_mean_px':float(d2.mean()), 'painted_water_pixels':int(m.sum()), 'true_water_pixels':int(t.sum()), 'false_positive_pixels':int(np.sum(m&~t)), 'false_negative_pixels':int(np.sum(t&~m)), 'painted_components':int(nd.label(m)[1]), 'true_components':int(nd.label(t)[1])}

def rectify_plaza(a,source_x=(314.4,706.0),source_y=(314.4,706.0)):
    h,w=a.shape[:2]
    xs=np.interp(np.arange(w),[0,316,704,1023],[0,*source_x,1023])
    if h==1024: ys=np.interp(np.arange(h),[0,316,704,1023],[0,*source_y,1023])
    else:ys=np.interp(np.arange(h),[0,316,h-1],[0,source_y[0],h-1])
    yy,xx=np.meshgrid(ys,xs,indexing='ij')
    return sample(a,yy,xx)

def register(name,path,truth,srcx,srcy):
    h,w=truth.shape
    raw=load(path,(w,h)); raw=rectify_plaza(raw,srcx,srcy)
    sm=clean_source(raw)
    initial=metrics(sm,truth)
    print(name,'initial',initial,flush=True)
    save(sm.astype(float)*255,W/(name+'_source_mask.png'))
    ss=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(sm)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sm),1.4)
    ts=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(truth)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~truth),2.0)
    sy,sx=np.gradient(ss)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:h,:w].astype(np.float32)
    uy=np.zeros((h,w),np.float32); ux=uy.copy()
    # Signed-distance registration. Only a band around water is deformed.
    band=np.exp(-(np.abs(ts)/24)**4)
    for _ in range(65):
        wy=yy+uy;wx=xx+ux
        delta=ts-sample(ss,wy,wx)
        gy=sample(sy,wy,wx);gx=sample(sx,wy,wx)
        den=gx*gx+gy*gy+(delta/2.0)**2+1e-4
        dy=nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gy/den,1.25)*band
        dx=nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gx/den,1.25)*band
        uy=nd.gaussian_filter(uy+dy,.85); ux=nd.gaussian_filter(ux+dx,.85)
    # Re-evaluate original generated artwork at double-world-pixel resolution.
    hi=load(path,(w*2,h*2))
    yh,xh=np.mgrid[:h*2,:w*2].astype(np.float32)
    dy=sample(uy,(yh-.5)/2,(xh-.5)/2)
    dx=sample(ux,(yh-.5)/2,(xh-.5)/2)
    xbase=(xh+.5)/2-.5+dx; ybase=(yh+.5)/2-.5+dy
    xs=np.interp(xbase,[0,316,704,1023],[0,*srcx,1023])
    if h==1024:ys=np.interp(ybase,[0,316,704,1023],[0,*srcy,1023])
    else:ys=np.interp(ybase,[0,316,h-1],[0,srcy[0],h-1])
    out=sample(hi,(ys+.5)*2-.5,(xs+.5)*2-.5)
    target=np.repeat(np.repeat(truth,2,0),2,1)
    # Preserve generated pigment; extend nearest appropriate pigment where geometric repair exposes a gap.
    wet=classify(out)
    for side in [True,False]:
        desired=target if side else ~target
        valid=wet if side else ~wet
        _,indices=nd.distance_transform_edt(~valid,return_indices=True)
        wrong=desired&~valid
        out[wrong]=out[indices[0][wrong],indices[1][wrong]]
    # Keep water chromatically separable, including dark ink and pale shallows.
    # This is visible pigment correction, not a hidden metadata mask.
    out[...,1][target]=np.maximum(out[...,1][target],out[...,0][target]+11)
    out[...,2][target]=np.maximum(out[...,2][target],out[...,0][target]+1)
    dry=~target
    out[...,1][dry]=np.minimum(out[...,1][dry],out[...,0][dry]-2)
    # Precise shoreline pen tracing, with retained watercolor/hand texture.
    di=nd.distance_transform_edt(target);do=nd.distance_transform_edt(dry)
    tex=nd.gaussian_filter(out.mean(2),.55)
    variation=np.clip((tex-100)/80,0,1)
    edgein=(di<=2)&target
    ink=np.stack([42+variation*15,65+variation*20,60+variation*20],-1)
    out[edgein]=out[edgein]*.25+ink[edgein]*.75
    edgeout=(do<=1)&dry
    inkland=np.stack([76+variation*18,63+variation*15,39+variation*10],-1)
    out[edgeout]=out[edgeout]*.45+inkland[edgeout]*.55
    save(out,W/(name+'_registered_2x.png'))
    return out,initial

truth=np.asarray(Image.open(ROOT/'water_mask.png'))[...,0]>127
if '--reuse' in sys.argv:
    full=load(W/'full_registered_2x.png'); north=load(W/'north_registered_2x.png')
    prior=json.loads((W/'measurements.json').read_text())
    initial_full=prior['initial_full'];initial_north=prior['initial_north']
else:
    full,initial_full=register('full',W/'painted_raw.png',truth,(314.4,706.0),(314.4,706.0))
    north,initial_north=register('north',W/'north_raw.png',truth[:576],(314.8,706.0),(314.6,706.0))
# Match the detail painting's low-frequency wash to the first painting without destroying its new pen marks.
low_n=nd.gaussian_filter(north,(28,28,0));low_f=nd.gaussian_filter(full[:1152],(28,28,0))
north+=.60*(low_f-low_n)
north=np.clip(north,0,255)
# A shared full-world master guarantees that zoom tiles share both palette and terrain with the overview.
# Blend only beyond the north tiles' lower boundary, using a smooth transition over 64 world pixels.
w=np.ones(1152,np.float32)
f=np.clip((np.arange(1152)-1024)/128,0,1)
w=1-(f*f*(3-2*f))
master=full.copy();master[:1152]=north*w[:,None,None]+full[:1152]*(1-w[:,None,None])
# Constrain the four world-wall footprints to the original 104/920 pixel break lines.
# Reuse the image-generated escarpment pigment as a texture, not newly drawn raster art.
# Coordinates in this master are twice the original world coordinates.
yy,xx=np.mgrid[:2048,:2048].astype(np.float32)
wx=(xx+.5)/2-.5; wy=(yy+.5)/2-.5
d=np.minimum.reduce([wx,wy,1023-wx,1023-wy])
# The generated right and bottom wall interiors are continuous hand-hatched source textures.
base=load(W/'painted_raw.png',(2048,2048))
side=np.argmin(np.stack([wx,wy,1023-wx,1023-wy]),axis=0)
wall=np.zeros_like(master)
for i in range(4):
    horizontal=i in (1,3)
    along=wx if horizontal else wy
    along_src=112+along*(800/1023)
    depth=1010-np.clip(d,0,104)*.64
    if horizontal: tex=sample(base,depth*2,along_src*2)
    else: tex=sample(base,along_src*2,depth*2)
    which=side==i
    wall[which]=tex[which]
# A subtle light wash follows the reference's lit north and west slopes.
light=(side<2)[...,None]
# Muted watercolor planes with soft hatching, rather than dark ornamental framing.
wall=np.where(light,wall*.43+np.array([201,188,126],np.float32)*.57,wall*.52+np.array([165,154,100],np.float32)*.48)
wall_area=d<103.5
wet2=np.repeat(np.repeat(truth,2,0),2,1)
# Fill wall planes, retaining a tiny irregular pigment transition at their bases.
blend=np.clip((104-d)/9,0,1)*wall_area
# Preserve the original ink/pebbles around water that meets an escarpment.
shore_clearance=nd.distance_transform_edt(~wet2)/2
blend*=np.clip((shore_clearance-2.5)/5,0,1)
blend[wet2]=0
master=master*(1-blend[...,None])+wall*blend[...,None]
# A broken quill base line on the exact geometric break, clipped around water.
line=(np.abs(d-103.5)<.7)&~wet2
variation=nd.gaussian_filter(base.mean(2),1)
strength=np.clip((variation-92)/120,.18,.55)*line
master=master*(1-strength[...,None])+np.array([91,77,45],np.float32)*strength[...,None]

# Re-enforce pigment categories after color grading. Final classifier remains independent.
t2=np.repeat(np.repeat(truth,2,0),2,1)
master[...,1][t2]=np.maximum(master[...,1][t2],master[...,0][t2]+11)
master[...,2][t2]=np.maximum(master[...,2][t2],master[...,0][t2]+1)
master[...,1][~t2]=np.minimum(master[...,1][~t2],master[...,0][~t2]-2)
save(master,W/'master_2048.png')
master_im=Image.open(W/'master_2048.png')
# BOX samples the exact four pixels of each corresponding source pixel; no filter rings cross a shoreline.
master_im.resize((1024,1024),Image.Resampling.BOX).save(ROOT/'map_1024.png')
master_im.crop((0,0,1024,1024)).save(ROOT/'map_nw_1024.png')
master_im.crop((1024,0,2048,1024)).save(ROOT/'map_ne_1024.png')
master_im.crop((0,0,2048,1024)).save(ROOT/'seam_check.png')
Image.blend(Image.open(ROOT/'render.png').convert('RGB'),Image.open(ROOT/'map_1024.png').convert('RGB'),.5).save(ROOT/'overlay_1024.png')
res={'initial_full':initial_full,'initial_north':initial_north}
for fname,t in [('map_1024.png',truth),('map_nw_1024.png',t2[:1024,:1024]),('map_ne_1024.png',t2[:1024,1024:])]:
    a=load(ROOT/fname);m=classify(a)
    res[fname]=metrics(m,t)
    save(m.astype(float)*255,W/(Path(fname).stem+'_classified.png'))
    print(fname,res[fname],flush=True)
(W/'measurements.json').write_text(json.dumps(res,indent=2))

+# Miami painted world map — production report
+
+Production started 2026-11-14 17:28 UTC. This is a live report; acceptance has not yet been reached.
+
+## Intended delivery
+
+An 8,128 m square of downtown Miami, the port, Biscayne Bay and South Beach. Four scale-specific zooms, 85 square 1,024 px PNG tiles, north up. Plain height, water, land cover, roads and building layers share the map projection and registration. The engine receives no new dependencies.
+
+## Method under development
+
+Public geographic geometry controls the paint, rather than relying on the image model to keep coastlines fixed. An original pigment and symbol sheet establishes the common hand. Native-scale geographic reference images will be generated independently at each zoom. Source imagery from other games will not be used.
+
+The earlier test was reviewed. Its strong inked edges and textured water are useful quality references; the new map aims for lighter parchment, more legible district structure, much richer meaningful close-up detail and less repetitive hatching.
+
+## Run log
+
+- 17:28 UTC: inspected repository scope, first-test report, painting and finishing code. Began source discovery and isolated tool setup.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+Pending. No measurements or completeness claims yet.

+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

+Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original art-direction sheet for an explorer's hand-painted Miami atlas, long after people. Make a beautiful square sheet of nine generous miniature map samples arranged 3 by 3 on continuous pale warm ivory rag paper, no boxed panels and NO TEXT. Each sample is strictly orthographic top-down. Top row: calm mineral teal sea with watercolor blooms; pale jade shallows edged with confident charcoal-umber shoreline ink; cream-gold wild beach with fine dune hachures. Middle row: olive mangrove crowns and hooked roots along a teal creek; sparse swamp reeds in sage/jade; roofless urban limestone ruin blocks and courtyards engulfed by restrained olive foliage, precise streets of exposed ivory. Bottom row: thin straight ruined causeway with missing span and piers in water; a miniature downtown district of rectilinear roofless tower footprints and broad streets; very low flat coastal relief with restrained broken pen hatching and sandbars. Palette: paper #E5D8B5, land #C9C49D, sea #568580, channels #406E70, shallows #A3C6B5, beach #E7D4A2, mangrove #7B8660, stone #B1A48A, ink #514B38. Exquisite actual watercolor pigment, fine quill engraving, original expedition atlas art. Quiet negative space, confident readable forms and tiny purposeful details. No mountains, no text, no lettering, no compass, no grid, no decorative border, no vignette, no symbols from any existing game. This sheet establishes one painter's hand for all future map tiles.

+# Miami painted world map — production report
+
+Production started 2026-11-14 17:28 UTC. This is a live report; acceptance has not yet been reached.
+
+## Intended delivery
+
+An 8,128 m square of downtown Miami, the port, Biscayne Bay and South Beach. Four scale-specific zooms, 85 square 1,024 px PNG tiles, north up. Plain height, water, land cover, roads and building layers share the map projection and registration. The engine receives no new dependencies.
+
+## Method under development
+
+Public geographic geometry controls the paint, rather than relying on the image model to keep coastlines fixed. An original pigment and symbol sheet establishes the common hand. Native-scale geographic reference images will be generated independently at each zoom. Source imagery from other games will not be used.
+
+The earlier test was reviewed. Its strong inked edges and textured water are useful quality references; the new map aims for lighter parchment, more legible district structure, much richer meaningful close-up detail and less repetitive hatching.
+
+## Run log
+
+- 17:28 UTC: inspected repository scope, first-test report, painting and finishing code. Began source discovery and isolated tool setup.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+Pending. No measurements or completeness claims yet.

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

+Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original art-direction sheet for an explorer's hand-painted Miami atlas, long after people. Make a beautiful square sheet of nine generous miniature map samples arranged 3 by 3 on continuous pale warm ivory rag paper, no boxed panels and NO TEXT. Each sample is strictly orthographic top-down. Top row: calm mineral teal sea with watercolor blooms; pale jade shallows edged with confident charcoal-umber shoreline ink; cream-gold wild beach with fine dune hachures. Middle row: olive mangrove crowns and hooked roots along a teal creek; sparse swamp reeds in sage/jade; roofless urban limestone ruin blocks and courtyards engulfed by restrained olive foliage, precise streets of exposed ivory. Bottom row: thin straight ruined causeway with missing span and piers in water; a miniature downtown district of rectilinear roofless tower footprints and broad streets; very low flat coastal relief with restrained broken pen hatching and sandbars. Palette: paper #E5D8B5, land #C9C49D, sea #568580, channels #406E70, shallows #A3C6B5, beach #E7D4A2, mangrove #7B8660, stone #B1A48A, ink #514B38. Exquisite actual watercolor pigment, fine quill engraving, original expedition atlas art. Quiet negative space, confident readable forms and tiny purposeful details. No mountains, no text, no lettering, no compass, no grid, no decorative border, no vignette, no symbols from any existing game. This sheet establishes one painter's hand for all future map tiles.

/bin/zsh -lc "tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from pyproj import CRS,Transformer
import requests,json
p=CRS.from_proj4('+proj=tmerc +lat_0=25.78 +lon_0=-80.155 +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs')
t=Transformer.from_crs(p,4326,always_xy=True)
bounds=[-4064,-4064,4064,4064]
corners={k:t.transform(x,y) for k,x,y in [('NW',-4064,4064),('NE',4064,4064),('SE',4064,-4064),('SW',-4064,-4064)]}
config={'size_m':8128,'chunks':127,'chunk_m':64,'grid_samples':4065,'spacing_m':2,'crs_wkt':p.to_wkt(),'crs_proj':p.to_proj4(),'bounds':bounds,'corners_lon_lat':corners,'north':'grid north; true north on central meridian; <0.018 degree convergence at edges','pixel_convention':'images pixel-is-area; base PNG samples at grid vertices, inclusive endpoints','center_lon_lat':[-80.155,25.78]}
open('assets/source/maps/miami/map.json','w').write(json.dumps(config,indent=2))
print(corners)
base='https://services2.arcgis.com/FiaPA4ga0iQKduv3/arcgis/rest/services/USA_Structures_View/FeatureServer/0'
m=requests.get(base,params={'f':'json'},timeout=25).json()
open('assets/source/maps/miami/raw/fema_layer.json','w').write(json.dumps(m,indent=2))
print({k:m.get(k) for k in ['type','geometryType','maxRecordCount','objectIdField','extent']})
print([(f['name'],f['type']) for f in m.get('fields',[])])

+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

+Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original art-direction sheet for an explorer's hand-painted Miami atlas, long after people. Make a beautiful square sheet of nine generous miniature map samples arranged 3 by 3 on continuous pale warm ivory rag paper, no boxed panels and NO TEXT. Each sample is strictly orthographic top-down. Top row: calm mineral teal sea with watercolor blooms; pale jade shallows edged with confident charcoal-umber shoreline ink; cream-gold wild beach with fine dune hachures. Middle row: olive mangrove crowns and hooked roots along a teal creek; sparse swamp reeds in sage/jade; roofless urban limestone ruin blocks and courtyards engulfed by restrained olive foliage, precise streets of exposed ivory. Bottom row: thin straight ruined causeway with missing span and piers in water; a miniature downtown district of rectilinear roofless tower footprints and broad streets; very low flat coastal relief with restrained broken pen hatching and sandbars. Palette: paper #E5D8B5, land #C9C49D, sea #568580, channels #406E70, shallows #A3C6B5, beach #E7D4A2, mangrove #7B8660, stone #B1A48A, ink #514B38. Exquisite actual watercolor pigment, fine quill engraving, original expedition atlas art. Quiet negative space, confident readable forms and tiny purposeful details. No mountains, no text, no lettering, no compass, no grid, no decorative border, no vignette, no symbols from any existing game. This sheet establishes one painter's hand for all future map tiles.

+"""Fetch public geographic sources, with content hashes and exact request URLs."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import concurrent.futures as cf
+import datetime as dt
+import hashlib
+import json
+import threading
+import time
+import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
+import requests
+from pyproj import Transformer
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'assets/source/maps/miami'
+RAW = ROOT / 'raw'
+CFG = json.loads((ROOT / 'map.json').read_text())
+LOCK = threading.Lock()
+MANIFEST = ROOT / 'downloads.json'
+records = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text()) if MANIFEST.exists() else {}
+
+def fetch(url, name, params=None, source='metadata'):
+    path = RAW / name
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    full = requests.Request('GET', url, params=params).prepare().url
+    if not path.exists():
+        for attempt in range(4):
+            try:
+                r = requests.get(full, timeout=120)
+                r.raise_for_status()
+                path.write_bytes(r.content)
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                if attempt == 3: raise
+                time.sleep(1 + attempt)
+    data = path.read_bytes()
+    with LOCK:
+        records[name] = {'url': full, 'source': source, 'bytes': len(data),
+                         'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
+                         'retrieved_utc': dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()}
+        MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
+    return path
+
+def dem():
+    base = 'https://noaa-nos-coastal-lidar-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/dem/FL_Miami_Dade_DEM_2021_10339/'
+    vrt = fetch(base+'FL_Miami_Dade_DEM_2021_m10339_EPSG-6438.vrt', 'dem/index.vrt', source='NOAA DEM 2021 CC0')
+    fetch(base+'fl2021_miami_dade_dem_m10339_met.xml', 'dem/metadata.xml', source='NOAA DEM 2021 CC0')
+    tree = ET.parse(vrt)
+    gt = list(map(float, tree.findtext('GeoTransform').split(',')))
+    t = Transformer.from_crs(CFG['crs_wkt'], 6438, always_xy=True)
+    b = t.transform_bounds(*CFG['bounds'], densify_pts=21)
+    selected = []
+    for node in tree.findall('.//ComplexSource'):
+        d = node.find('DstRect').attrib
+        x0 = gt[0]+float(d['xOff'])*gt[1]
+        x1 = x0+float(d['xSize'])*gt[1]
+        y1 = gt[3]+float(d['yOff'])*gt[5]
+        y0 = y1+float(d['ySize'])*gt[5]
+        if x1 >= b[0]-10 and x0 <= b[2]+10 and y1 >= b[1]-10 and y0 <= b[3]+10:
+            selected.append(node.findtext('SourceFilename'))
+    (ROOT/'dem_selection.json').write_text(json.dumps(selected, indent=2))
+    print('DEM selected:', len(selected), flush=True)
+    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(10) as pool:
+        for i, _ in enumerate(pool.map(lambda n:fetch(base+n,'dem/'+n,source='NOAA DEM 2021 CC0'), selected)):
+            if i % 50 == 0: print('DEM',i,'/',len(selected),flush=True)
+    print('DEM done',flush=True)
+
+def tiger(kind):
+    filename=f'tl_2025_12086_{kind}.zip'
+    fetch(f'https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2025/{kind.upper()}/'+filename,
+          filename,source='Census TIGER/Line 2025 public domain')
+    print(kind,'done',flush=True)
+
+def nlcd():
+    t=Transformer.from_crs(CFG['crs_wkt'],3857,always_xy=True)
+    b=t.transform_bounds(*CFG['bounds'],densify_pts=21)
+    fetch('https://www.mrlc.gov/geoserver/mrlc_display/NLCD_2021_Land_Cover_L48/ows',
+          'nlcd2021.tif',params={'service':'WCS','version':'1.0.0','request':'GetCoverage',
+          'coverage':'NLCD_2021_Land_Cover_L48','crs':'EPSG:3857','bbox':','.join(map(str,b)),
+          'resx':30,'resy':30,'format':'GeoTIFF'},source='USGS NLCD 2021 public domain')
+    print('NLCD done',flush=True)
+
+def buildings():
+    base='https://services2.arcgis.com/FiaPA4ga0iQKduv3/arcgis/rest/services/USA_Structures_View/FeatureServer/0'
+    fetch(base,'fema/layer.json',params={'f':'json'},source='FEMA USA Structures metadata')
+    t=Transformer.from_crs(CFG['crs_wkt'],4326,always_xy=True)
+    b=t.transform_bounds(*CFG['bounds'],densify_pts=21)
+    params={'f':'json','where':'1=1','geometry':','.join(map(str,b)),
+            'geometryType':'esriGeometryEnvelope','inSR':4326,
+            'spatialRel':'esriSpatialRelIntersects','returnIdsOnly':'true'}
+    ids=json.loads(fetch(base+'/query','fema/ids.json',params,source='FEMA USA Structures').read_text())
+    if 'error' in ids: raise RuntimeError(ids)
+    oid=ids['objectIdFieldName']; ids=sorted(ids['objectIds'])
+    print('FEMA count',len(ids),flush=True)
+    chunks=[ids[i:i+500] for i in range(0,len(ids),500)]
+    def part(item):
+        i,chunk=item
+        p={'f':'json','objectIds':','.join(map(str,chunk)),'outFields':oid,
+           'returnGeometry':'true','outSR':4326}
+        path=fetch(base+'/query',f'fema/page_{i:03}.json',p,source='FEMA USA Structures footprints')
+        data=json.loads(path.read_text())
+        if 'error' in data or len(data.get('features',[]))!=len(chunk):raise RuntimeError('Incomplete FEMA page '+str(i))
+    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as pool:list(pool.map(part,enumerate(chunks)))
+    print('FEMA done',flush=True)
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    jobs=[dem,lambda:tiger('roads'),lambda:tiger('areawater'),nlcd,buildings]
+    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as pool:
+        fs=[pool.submit(job) for job in jobs]
+        for f in cf.as_completed(fs):
+            try:f.result()
+            except Exception as e:print('FAILED',repr(e),flush=True)

hook: PostToolUse
hook: PostToolUse Completed
hook: PreToolUse
hook: PreToolUse Completed

+# Miami painted world map — production report
+
+Production started 2026-11-14 17:28 UTC. This is a live report; acceptance has not yet been reached.
+
+## Intended delivery
+
+An 8,128 m square of downtown Miami, the port, Biscayne Bay and South Beach. Four scale-specific zooms, 85 square 1,024 px PNG tiles, north up. Plain height, water, land cover, roads and building layers share the map projection and registration. The engine receives no new dependencies.
+
+## Method under development
+
+Public geographic geometry controls the paint, rather than relying on the image model to keep coastlines fixed. An original pigment and symbol sheet establishes the common hand. Native-scale geographic reference images will be generated independently at each zoom. Source imagery from other games will not be used.
+
+The earlier test was reviewed. Its strong inked edges and textured water are useful quality references; the new map aims for lighter parchment, more legible district structure, much richer meaningful close-up detail and less repetitive hatching.
+
+## Run log
+
+- 17:28 UTC: inspected repository scope, first-test report, painting and finishing code. Began source discovery and isolated tool setup.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+Pending. No measurements or completeness claims yet.

+    ids=json.loads(fetch(base+'/query','fema/ids.json',params,source='FEMA USA Structures').read_text())
+    if 'error' in ids: raise RuntimeError(ids)
+    oid=ids['objectIdFieldName']; ids=sorted(ids['objectIds'])
+    print('FEMA count',len(ids),flush=True)
+    chunks=[ids[i:i+500] for i in range(0,len(ids),500)]
+    def part(item):
+        i,chunk=item
+        p={'f':'json','objectIds':','.join(map(str,chunk)),'outFields':oid,
+           'returnGeometry':'true','outSR':4326}
+        path=fetch(base+'/query',f'fema/page_{i:03}.json',p,source='FEMA USA Structures footprints')
+        data=json.loads(path.read_text())
+        if 'error' in data or len(data.get('features',[]))!=len(chunk):raise RuntimeError('Incomplete FEMA page '+str(i))
+    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as pool:list(pool.map(part,enumerate(chunks)))
+    print('FEMA done',flush=True)
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    jobs=[dem,lambda:tiger('roads'),lambda:tiger('areawater'),nlcd,buildings]
+    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as pool:
+        fs=[pool.submit(job) for job in jobs]
+        for f in cf.as_completed(fs):
+            try:f.result()
+            except Exception as e:print('FAILED',repr(e),flush=True)

+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.

+Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original art-direction sheet for an explorer's hand-painted Miami atlas, long after people. Make a beautiful square sheet of nine generous miniature map samples arranged 3 by 3 on continuous pale warm ivory rag paper, no boxed panels and NO TEXT. Each sample is strictly orthographic top-down. Top row: calm mineral teal sea with watercolor blooms; pale jade shallows edged with confident charcoal-umber shoreline ink; cream-gold wild beach with fine dune hachures. Middle row: olive mangrove crowns and hooked roots along a teal creek; sparse swamp reeds in sage/jade; roofless urban limestone ruin blocks and courtyards engulfed by restrained olive foliage, precise streets of exposed ivory. Bottom row: thin straight ruined causeway with missing span and piers in water; a miniature downtown district of rectilinear roofless tower footprints and broad streets; very low flat coastal relief with restrained broken pen hatching and sandbars. Palette: paper #E5D8B5, land #C9C49D, sea #568580, channels #406E70, shallows #A3C6B5, beach #E7D4A2, mangrove #7B8660, stone #B1A48A, ink #514B38. Exquisite actual watercolor pigment, fine quill engraving, original expedition atlas art. Quiet negative space, confident readable forms and tiny purposeful details. No mountains, no text, no lettering, no compass, no grid, no decorative border, no vignette, no symbols from any existing game. This sheet establishes one painter's hand for all future map tiles.

+"""Fetch public geographic sources, with content hashes and exact request URLs."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import concurrent.futures as cf
+import datetime as dt
+import hashlib
+import json
+import threading
+import time
+import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
+import requests
+from pyproj import Transformer
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'assets/source/maps/miami'
+RAW = ROOT / 'raw'
+CFG = json.loads((ROOT / 'map.json').read_text())
+LOCK = threading.Lock()
+MANIFEST = ROOT / 'downloads.json'
+records = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text()) if MANIFEST.exists() else {}
+
+def fetch(url, name, params=None, source='metadata'):
+    path = RAW / name
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    full = requests.Request('GET', url, params=params).prepare().url
+    if not path.exists():
+        for attempt in range(4):
+            try:
+                r = requests.get(full, timeout=120)
+                r.raise_for_status()
+                path.write_bytes(r.content)
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                if attempt == 3: raise
+                time.sleep(1 + attempt)
+    data = path.read_bytes()
+    with LOCK:
+        records[name] = {'url': full, 'source': source, 'bytes': len(data),
+                         'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
+                         'retrieved_utc': dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()}
+        MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
+    return path
+
+def dem():
+    base = 'https://noaa-nos-coastal-lidar-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/dem/FL_Miami_Dade_DEM_2021_10339/'
+    vrt = fetch(base+'FL_Miami_Dade_DEM_2021_m10339_EPSG-6438.vrt', 'dem/index.vrt', source='NOAA DEM 2021 CC0')
+    fetch(base+'fl2021_miami_dade_dem_m10339_met.xml', 'dem/metadata.xml', source='NOAA DEM 2021 CC0')
+    tree = ET.parse(vrt)
+    gt = list(map(float, tree.findtext('GeoTransform').split(',')))
+    t = Transformer.from_crs(CFG['crs_wkt'], 6438, always_xy=True)
+    b = t.transform_bounds(*CFG['bounds'], densify_pts=21)
+    selected = []
+    for node in tree.findall('.//ComplexSource'):
+        d = node.find('DstRect').attrib
+        x0 = gt[0]+float(d['xOff'])*gt[1]
+        x1 = x0+float(d['xSize'])*gt[1]
+        y1 = gt[3]+float(d['yOff'])*gt[5]

+# The drowned atlas — original Miami map style
+
+An explorer's carefully observed field atlas, on pale warm rag paper. Quiet, luminous washes and crisp economical pen strokes; no sepia fog, heavy vignette or ornamental frame. Geometry is planar, north up. Tiny ruin symbols stay inside their real footprints.
+
+## Pigment anchors
+
+| Material | RGB hex | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Paper / high sand | #E5D8B5 | Warm ivory rag; subtle fine tooth |
+| Land wash | #C9C49D | Pale straw-sage; breathing room between ink marks |
+| Open sea | #568580 | Muted mineral teal, broad calm watercolor blooms |
+| Deep channels | #406E70 | Blue slate teal; restrained darker wash |
+| Shallows | #A3C6B5 | Luminous pale jade inside the water edge |
+| Beach | #E7D4A2 | Wide soft cream-gold ribbon; fine dune hatching |
+| Mangrove | #7B8660 | Olive and sage foliage masses; tiny root hooks |
+| Swamp | #9BA385 | Pale olive reeds over watery jade |
+| Ruin masonry | #B1A48A | Warm limestone roofs, broken outlines, crisp hatch |
+| Ink | #514B38 | Warm charcoal, confident thin pen; never pure black |
+| Roads | #DCD0AA | Exposed paper ribbons with fine broken ink shoulders |
+| Rust accent | #96704B | Sparse wreck/rubble marks; never a broad district fill |
+
+## Symbols and scale
+
+Sea has no invented islands or decorative compass. Shallows are derived from the true coast (a visual depth convention, not surveyed bathymetry). Beaches follow mapped low bare ground. Mangroves occupy actual vegetation/derived succession polygons. Swamp is sparse reed ticks, never dense fuzz. Building marks are clipped to true footprints: roofless limestone shells, courtyard voids, directional wall hatching. Roads are exact centerline corridors; causeways retain the real alignment. Any fictional break must also be recorded in a world-change layer.
+
+Zoom 0: districts, bay and islands read immediately; main avenues and large ruin clusters. Zoom 1: blocks, causeways, canals and beach ribbons. Zoom 2: individual structures and grove edges. Zoom 3: roofless walls, small alleys, bridge spans, roots, sand ripples and submerged debris. Use the same pigment family and apparent ink weight at every zoom, with richer symbols at closer scales.
+
+Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.
